children: Gap's Old Navy brand is regaining engagement from low- and middle-income shoppers thanks to its denim offerings, Chief Executive Michael Francis says on a call with investors. During the fall, the company's denim and knits categories were especially strong, Francis says. Old Navy introduced a wider assortment of styles and choices. Its denim business moved from number three to number two most popular among denim retailers in the U.S., Francis says. Denim was also the top search term on Old Navy's website, he says. Old Navy same-store sales were flat, but continue to make up the biggest portion of Gap's total revenue. Gap shares rise 4% after hours. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)
